method.method_draft: Use an inertial ground-frame Newton’s-second-law analysis. First read the image: the cart compartment is horizontal, ball A hangs from the roof with the string tilted 45° from the vertical toward the left, and box B touches the left vertical wall while resting on the smooth floor. From the text take m1=2 kg, m2=5 kg, g=10 m/s^2, the 45° string angle, and that A and B are stationary relative to the accelerating cart. Since A is fixed relative to the cart, its horizontal acceleration equals the cart acceleration and its vertical acceleration is zero. Draw the force diagram for A in the inertial frame: tension T along the string and weight m1g downward. Resolve forces: vertical balance gives T cos45°=m1g, and horizontal dynamics gives T sin45°=m1a. Hence T=20√2 N and a=g tan45°=10 m/s^2. For B, the smooth floor supplies no horizontal force; the side wall normal is the only horizontal force accelerating B with the cart, so N=m2a=50 N. By Newton’s third law, B exerts the same magnitude pressure on the wall.
